evals.prompt: Our web application has multiple issues: the main video player clips outside the container on window resize, and clicking the model filter resets the selection with an error. Walk me through debugging and fixing both issues.
evals.expected_output: Prompts via ask_question Pre-Flight Gate (if mode ambiguous), reproduces empirically using run_diagnose.py, constructs a Symptom-to-Root-Cause Matrix, applies surgical fixes, proves resolution via closed-loop re-run, and produces a Markdown Artifact with RequestFeedback: true.
expectations: Enforces the 4-step workflow: Pre-Flight Gate, Reproduce First, Symptom-to-Root-Cause Matrix, and Surgical Fix & Verify
Uses ask_question to offer choices between Live Chrome Tab, Headless Background Sandbox, and Backend & Runtime Only when mode is not specified
Captures empirical proof via run_diagnose.py before modifying any code
Constructs a Symptom-to-Root-Cause Matrix mapping each symptom to failing evidence, root cause, file/line, and verification check
Employs Dual Output reporting by generating a structured Markdown Artifact for complex multi-symptom bugs

evals.prompt: I have Chrome open right now on http://localhost:8000 looking at our app, and the video canvas is overflowing the layout horizontally. Debug the live tab, find the CSS causing the overflow, and fix it.
evals.expected_output: Detects user's explicit preference for the live tab, skips ask_question, executes run_diagnose.py ui --live --audit-layout to measure bounding boxes, identifies root cause, fixes layout defensively, and verifies resolution.
expectations: Skips ask_question because user explicitly requested live tab inspection
Executes run_diagnose.py ui with --live and --audit-layout to inspect live DOM bounding boxes and layout overflows via CDP
Applies defensive CSS containment (such as min-width: 0 or overflow containment) without breaking layout rules
Re-runs layout inspection post-fix to achieve closed-loop verification with hasOverflow: false

evals.prompt: Our Docker backend is crashing on startup with a 500 error, and the CPU is pegged at 100%. I suspect the container is running stale code that was not updated. Diagnose and resolve this container failure.
evals.expected_output: Executes run_diagnose.py container with --lines and --sync-check to inspect tracebacks and verify host-vs-container MD5 sync, isolates the failing traceback, and verifies the runtime fix.
expectations: Executes run_diagnose.py container with --sync-check to detect host-vs-container MD5 file drift
Scans recent container logs for unhandled Tracebacks and exceptions using --lines
Diagnoses whether the crash is caused by code drift or runtime loop without speculative edits
Verifies container health and reports status under Axiom 9 Honest Verification Reporting

evals.prompt: After our recent HTML cleanup, clicking the submit button throws a ReferenceError in the console. Scan the surface for broken element IDs and event handlers, map the root cause, and fix the script.
evals.expected_output: Executes run_diagnose.py surface --show-ids to compare HTML element IDs against JavaScript queries, maps the broken ID in the Symptom Matrix, repairs the selector, and runs tests.
expectations: Executes run_diagnose.py surface --show-ids to statically inventory HTML element IDs and interactive controls
Identifies mismatch between DOM element ID and JavaScript query selector or event listener
Maps symptom to root cause in the Symptom-to-Root-Cause Matrix with exact target file and line
Runs unit test suite via run_diagnose.py tests to confirm zero regressions

expectations: Follows Dual Output rules by providing a concise inline Markdown response for simple single-step bugs
Avoids unnecessary artifact creation overhead for simple single-symptom bug fixes
